entities.summary: In architecture, "Romano-Gothic" is a term for an architectural style, part of Early Gothic architecture, which evolved in Europe in the 12th century CE from the Romanesque style, and was an early style in Gothic architecture. In England "Early English Gothic" remains the usual term. The style is characterized by rounded and pointed arches on a vertical plane. Flying buttresses were used, but are mainly undecorated. Romanesque buttresses were also used. Romano-Gothic began to use the decorative elements of Gothic architecture, but not the constructional principles of more fully Gothic buildings.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Romano-Gothic architectural style played a significant role in shaping the medieval landscape of Southern Europe, influencing building designs and construction techniques that endured for centuries. Its use of rounded and pointed arches and flying buttresses contributed to the development of Gothic architecture.
